{"id": "0eaa7055-6a57-4b16-83de-852125babde0", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_i7DkhiXtlnezV0HgSWoSxq", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Quotas for the bedrock-runtime endpoint\",\"context\":\"## Requesting a quota increase\\n\\nThe steps for requesting a quota increase for your account depend on the value in the **Adjustable** column in the quotas table in Amazon Bedrock service quotas.\\n\\n**Important:**\\n\\nBefore requesting a quota increase, verify that the model is not in a *Legacy* or *Deprecated* lifecycle status. Quota increases are not granted for models that are scheduled for retirement. Check the model's lifecycle status on the Model lifecycle page and consider migrating to the successor model instead.\\n\\n* If a quota is marked as **Yes**, you can adjust it by following the steps at Requesting a Quota Increase in the Service Quotas User Guide.\\n* For any model, you can request an increase for the following quotas together:\\n\\n + Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute for `${model}`\\n + On-demand InvokeModel tokens per minute for `${model}`\\n + Cross-Model Max Tokens Per Day\\n\\n To request an increase for any combination of these quotas, request an increase for the **Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute for `${model}`** quota by following the steps at Requesting a Quota Increase in the Service Quotas User Guide. After you do so, the support team will reach out and offer you the option of also increasing the other two quotas.\\n\\n **Note:**\\n\\n Due to overwhelming demand, priority will be given to customers who generate traffic that consumes their existing quota allocation. Your request might be denied if you don't meet this condition.\\n\\nFor `bedrock-mantle` quota increases, see Requesting a quota increase\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-runtime.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"How do I troubleshoot the \\\"ThrottlingException\\\" error when I use Amazon Bedrock on-demand resources?\",\"context\":\"### Request a quota increase\\n\\nNew AWS accounts might have lower initial quotas than the default quotas. Specific models have non-adjustable fixed quotas. If your workload traffic exceeds your account's on-demand quotas, then contact [AWS Support](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/case-management.html#creating-a-support-case) or your account manager to [request a quota increase](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-increase.html). AWS might adjust default quotas based on usage patterns or service requirements.\\n\\nInclude the following information in your request:\\n\\n* The name of the quota to increase\\n* Your current quota value and the quota value that you require\\n* The model ID\\n* The Region for the quota increase\\n* A brief explanation of your use case\\n* Your projected usage, including steady and peak tokens and requests per minute, and average input and output tokens per request\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/bedrock-throttling-error\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"Troubleshooting Amazon Bedrock API Error Codes\",\"context\":\"## ThrottlingException\\n\\n**HTTP Status Code:** 429\\n\\n**Cause:** The request was denied due to exceeding the account quotas for Amazon Bedrock.\\n\\n**Solution:**\\n\\n* Check the Amazon Bedrock service quotas in the Amazon Bedrock service quotas console to learn about the limits allotted to your account.\\n* We suggest employing AWS recommended approach of using retries with exponential backoff.\\n and random jitter for improved reliability.\\n* If you have predictable, sustained throughput requirements, consider Reserved Tier or Provisioned Throughput, depending on what your model supports. Availability varies by model and AWS Region. Check the model's detail page for Reserved Tier support and the Provisioned Throughput support table for availability. To access Reserved Tier, contact your AWS account team.\\n* Request for quota increase by contacting your account manager or AWS Support if your workload traffic exceeds your account quotas\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/troubleshooting-api-error-codes.html\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"bedrockruntime\",\"context\":\"## type ThrottlingException \\n\\n```\\ntype ThrottlingException struct {\\n RespMetadata protocol.ResponseMetadata `json:\\\"-\\\" xml:\\\"-\\\"`\\n\\n Message_ *string `locationName:\\\"message\\\" type:\\\"string\\\"`\\n // contains filtered or unexported fields\\n}\\n```\\n\\nYour request was throttled because of service-wide limitations. Resubmit\\nyour request later or in a different region. You can also purchase Provisioned\\nThroughput (<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prov-throughput.html>)\\nto increase the rate or number of tokens you can process\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-go/api/service/bedrockruntime/index.html\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"Quotas for the bedrock-mantle endpoint\",\"context\":\"## How requests are evaluated against quotas\\n\\nWhen you submit an inference request to the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint, AWS evaluates it against your quotas in the following order:\\n\\n1. **Input tokens per minute** \u2013 The number of input tokens in the request, plus the value of `max_tokens` (or the model-specific maximum if `max_tokens` is not set), is checked against the input-tokens-per-minute quota for the requested model. If admitting the request would exceed the quota, the request is throttled with an HTTP 429 response.\\n2. **Output tokens per minute** \u2013 As the model streams or generates output, output tokens are counted against the output-tokens-per-minute quota for that model. If the quota is reached during generation, generation stops and the response is returned with a finish reason indicating the cutoff.\\n\\nAfter the response completes, any unused portion of the initial input-token reservation (the difference between `max_tokens` and the actual output) is replenished to your quota.\\n\\nThe endpoint may apply additional internal rate limiting that is not exposed in Service Quotas. Use retry logic with exponential backoff to handle transient throttling.\\n\\nThe `bedrock-runtime` endpoint's TPM quotas count input and output tokens together against a single per-model quota, while the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint applies separate input-tokens-per-minute and output-tokens-per-minute quotas. If you run workloads on both endpoints, plan capacity for each endpoint independently. For details on the runtime endpoint's quotas, see Quotas for the bedrock-runtime endpoint\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-mantle.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Look up Bedrock quota increase documentation"}

{"id": "6e89925b-9a91-42dc-b833-91dc2b559c0a", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "There are two ways to raise the quota, and both start with checking whether the quota can be adjusted.

**1. Request an increase in Service Quotas**
- Open Service Quotas, choose **Amazon Bedrock**, and find the quota for your model and Region. For example, "On-demand InvokeModel tokens per minute for `<model>`" or "Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute for `<model>`".
- If the **Adjustable** column says **Yes**, select the quota and choose **Request increase at account level**.
- To raise the on-demand, cross-Region and daily tokens quotas together, request the increase on **Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute for `<model>`**. AWS Support will then offer to raise the other two as well.

**2. Open an AWS Support case, or contact your account manager**
This applies if the quota isn't adjustable, or if you want to discuss capacity. Include:
- The quota name, your current value and the value you need
- The model ID and Region
- Your use case
- Projected steady and peak requests per minute and tokens per minute, plus average input and output tokens per request

**Things that affect whether it's approved**
- AWS gives priority to accounts that already use most of their current quota. A request can be denied if your traffic doesn't consume the existing allocation.
- Quota increases aren't granted for models in *Legacy* or *Deprecated* status. Check the model's lifecycle status and consider moving to its successor.
- New accounts often start with lower quotas, and some models have fixed quotas that can't be changed.

**While you wait for the increase**
- Add retries with exponential backoff and jitter. AWS recommends this for ThrottlingException (HTTP 429).
- Use cross-Region inference profiles to spread load across Regions.
- For steady, predictable throughput, consider Provisioned Throughput. Reserved Tier is available for some models through your account team.
- Check the quota against your real token usage. `max_tokens` is counted against quota when a request is admitted. A very high `max_tokens` can cause throttling even when actual output is small, so lowering it can help.

I can look up your current Bedrock quota values and recent usage in CloudWatch to size the request. To do that, I need the model ID, the Region and the AWS account ID.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
